Securities Clarity Act. Operative text amends the
securities laws to carve investment contract assets
out of the definition of a security, addressed on its
face to digital assets raised through blockchain-based
protocols. Digital-asset market structure is core
category subject matter.

SECURE Notarization Act of 2022 -- the measure named
in this category's agenda. Operative text authorises
notaries public to perform electronic and remote
notarizations for remotely located individuals and
compels Federal and State recognition. Remote online
notarization is an enumerated category term.

Securities Clarity Act (117th). Operative text
excludes investment contract assets from the security
definition, expressly for digital assets and
blockchain-based protocols. Digital-asset market
structure is core category subject matter.

Cryptocurrency Tax Clarity Act. Operative text amends
IRC s.6045 to define 'digital asset' as value recorded
on a cryptographically secured distributed ledger and
to treat digital assets as specified securities for
broker reporting. The regulated instrument is the
digital asset itself.

Official short title 'Small LENDER Act' and official
long title 'Small Lenders Exempt from New Data and
Excessive Reporting Act' state the operative effect:
exempting smaller lenders from the CFPB
small-business-lending data collection under
ECOA/Dodd-Frank section 1071. Credit unions are
covered financial institutions under that rule, so the
measure carries a material credit-union policy nexus.
Category is corroborated inside the north-star corpus
itself: the same bill family in other Congresses
(118:hr:1806, 119:hr:941, same sponsor and same
official title) is held in discovery under
member_business_lending and
cfpb_issues_structural_reform, and discovery routes
CFPB section 1071 Regulation B rule disapprovals
(118:hjres:50, 118:sjres:32) to
member_business_lending. ACU's own advocacy record
files section 1071 both as Consumer Protection (letter
1591 on S.557) and as Lending (letter 3441 on the CFPB
1071 rule). The legacy Member Business Lending
category is therefore retained and
cfpb_issues_structural_reform is added, not
substituted. Operative bill text was not reviewed: no
BillStatus receipt, GovInfo object or discovery record
for this key is held locally and network collection is
barred.

Official title is dispositive of subject:
congressional disapproval under 5 U.S.C. ch. 8 of a
Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection rule under
Truth in Lending (Regulation Z) governing use of
digital user accounts to access Buy Now, Pay Later
loans. Credit unions are Regulation Z creditors, and
America's Credit Unions filed its own comment letter
on this exact rule (letter 1126, 'Comment Letter to
CFPB on BNPL Digital User Accounts', 2024-07-31),
which ACU classifies under its Consumer Protection
issue area -- establishing the credit-union policy
nexus and placing the measure in the outline's
Consumer Protection section, not Payment & Technology.
The legacy 'Payments' category is unsupported: the
north-star Payments boundary is real-time payments,
FedNow, instant payment fraud, payment system access,
ACH payment, faster payments and payment stablecoin,
none of which a Regulation Z consumer-credit rule
touches; the legacy retrieval URL shows the measure
was pulled in by a legacy Payments query containing a
loose 'buy now pay later' term that the
outline-derived Payments query does not carry.
Discovery's own routing of CFPB rule disapprovals by
the rule's subject (Regulation Z credit card penalty
fees -> credit_card_consumer_fee_mandates at
118:hjres:121 and 118:sjres:70) and ACU's parallel
disapproval letters (396, 1581) fix the corrected
categories. Operative text was not reviewed: no
BillStatus receipt, GovInfo object or discovery record
for this key is held locally.
